title: Validate a person in its compact constructor

blocks.text: A record's **compact constructor** runs before the component fields are assigned, so it is the one place to validate a record's input: every `new` of the record goes through it.
public record Person(String name, int age)
so that a `Person` can only be created with valid data:

items: a `name` that is `null` or empty (`""`) is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message is `Name cannot be null or empty`;
a negative `age` is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message is `Age cannot be negative`;
everything else is accepted unchanged. Leave the generated accessors, `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString` alone.

blocks.text:
new Person("Alice", 30)          -> name() = "Alice", age() = 30, prints Person[name=Alice, age=30]
new Person(null, 20)             -> IllegalArgumentException: Name cannot be null or empty
new Person("", 20)               -> IllegalArgumentException: Name cannot be null or empty
new Person("Eve", -1)            -> IllegalArgumentException: Age cannot be negative
new Person("Baby", 0)            -> a valid person

cases.says: A valid person keeps its name and age, and prints as Person[name=Alice, age=30].
A null name is refused with IllegalArgumentException, not a NullPointerException.
An empty name is refused with IllegalArgumentException.
A negative age is refused with IllegalArgumentException.
An age of zero is a valid age.

concepts: A compact constructor validates the components, and every construction of the record goes through it.
A record declaration generates a canonical constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode and a Person[name=Alice, age=30] toString.
